editorial.thesis: A motor-trade-and-banking city of about 366,000. Its retail is heavy on banks & atms and grocery & daily needs, and thin on coaching & training and fitness & wellness — and 26% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 33% of Hyderabad's. 10.93 chain outlets per lakh residents against 33.58 in Hyderabad; 18 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Apollo Pharmacy 10, Bata 4, Reliance Digital 4.

The mapped economy leans to automotive. Shares of all mapped places: automotive 5.6% (Hyderabad 3.1%); banks & finance 13.3% (Hyderabad 8.1%); offices 5.7% (Hyderabad 10.9%); hotels & stays 2.1% (Hyderabad 3.8%). Raw counts would mislead because Hyderabad is mapped more completely (62,819 places against 1,641), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 2 zones hold 26% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Kanteshwar alone has about 56,000 residents and 10 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is more concentrated than in Hyderabad. 58% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Hyderabad 43%). The largest cores are Kotagalli · Shivajinagar (567 places) and Mjp Nagar (181).

The widest brand gaps against Hyderabad. Apollo Pharmacy 10 outlets vs 348; MedPlus 3 outlets vs 150; Reliance Trends 2 outlets vs 89. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 6 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Hyderabad, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Kotagalli · Shivajinagar and Kanteshwar are the largest zones by residents (180,000 and 56,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 58% of all commercial places, and Kotagalli · Shivajinagar alone lists 567.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Kotagalli · Shivajinagar holds 21 of the 40 tracked chain outlets, and Mjp Nagar adds 8.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Kotagalli · Shivajinagar and Kanteshwar lead on education places (42 and 19, with 7 and 1 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Kanteshwar and Dharmaram. The blue cores include Kotagalli · Shivajinagar.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (62,819 places in Hyderabad against 1,641 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Hyderabad; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Hyderabad, Nizamabad's mapped places over-index on automotive (5.6% vs 3.1%), banks & finance (13.3% vs 8.1%), healthcare (13.8% vs 10.3%) and under-index on offices (5.7% vs 10.9%), hotels & stays (2.1% vs 3.8%), services & crafts (4.3% vs 6.9%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 40 outlets of 18 tracked national brands within 6 km — 10.93 per lakh residents against Hyderabad's 33.58 (1440 outlets of 44 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Hyderabad are Apollo Pharmacy (10 vs 348); MedPlus (3 vs 150); Reliance Trends (2 vs 89). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Hyderabad's, so low means thin by Hyderabad's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 6 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Nizamabad's age mix against Hyderabad: children (0–14) 22.5% vs 24.6%, 15–24 19.3% vs 20.4%, working age 48.3% vs 48.0%, 60+ 10.0% vs 7.0%. Under-25s are 42% of residents.

zones.503001: About 180,000 residents, 567 mapped places (retail depth index 94), 21 chain outlets.
zones.503002: An under-served zone: about 56,000 residents, 100 mapped places, 10 food & drink and 5 chain outlets. Depth index 53.
zones.503003: About 55,000 residents, 181 mapped places (retail depth index 99), 8 chain outlets.
zones.503230: An under-served zone: about 25,000 residents, 42 mapped places, 1 food & drink and 3 chain outlets. Depth index 51.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 3.8% of mapped places against 5.0% in Hyderabad — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: KFC 2 (Hyderabad 49), Domino's 1 (Hyderabad 85), Pizza Hut 1 (Hyderabad 41). No mapped outlet in either city: Biryani By Kilo, Faasos.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 1.3% of mapped places against 2.3% in Hyderabad — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Third Wave Coffee 1 (Hyderabad 2). No mapped outlet in either city: Chaayos, Chai Sutta Bar.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 1.0% of mapped places against 0.8% in Hyderabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 1 (Hyderabad 29).
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 2.7% of mapped places against 2.1% in Hyderabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 2 (Hyderabad 42), More 2 (Hyderabad 18), Vishal Mega Mart 1 (Hyderabad 10). No mapped outlet in either city: Easyday.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.1% of mapped places against 1.3% in Hyderabad — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 10 (Hyderabad 348), MedPlus 3 (Hyderabad 150). No mapped outlet in either city: Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 7.3% of mapped places against 5.8% in Hyderabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 4 (Hyderabad 70), Reliance Trends 2 (Hyderabad 89), Raymond 2 (Hyderabad 37), Max Fashion 1 (Hyderabad 15).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 13.3% of mapped places against 8.1% in Hyderabad — above its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 0.8% of mapped places against 2.8% in Hyderabad — below its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 1.8% of mapped places against 3.5% in Hyderabad — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
